questions.scenario: A data platform team built an internal MCP server, `warehouse`, for a developer-productivity assistant. It exposes only tools: `list_datasets`, `describe_dataset(name)`, and `run_query(sql)`. Telemetry over 1,200 questions shows the agent makes 6 to 9 calls per question before the first `run_query`, almost all of them `list_datasets` and `describe_dataset` on tables it ends up not using; median latency is 48 seconds. The 140 dataset schemas change about once a week. The team wants the agent to know what data exists without spending calls discovering it. What should they change in the server?
options: Add a `get_all_schemas` tool that returns all 140 schemas in one call, and tell the agent in the system prompt to call it at the start of every question.
Expose the dataset catalog and each schema as MCP resources, so the host provides them as context instead of the model discovering them with tool calls.
Paste the full catalog of datasets and their columns into the `run_query` tool description, so the model sees every table before deciding what to query.
Raise the agent's turn limit and allow parallel tool calls, so the exploratory `describe_dataset` calls run at the same time and stop adding latency.
questions.why_correct: Los resources son fuentes de datos pasivas, de solo lectura, para dar contexto (el ejemplo de la doc incluye schemas de bases de datos), y los controla la aplicación, no el modelo. Exponer el catálogo como resources le da al agente visibilidad de los datos disponibles sin tool calls exploratorias, que es exactamente lo que describe la guía del examen.

why_wrong.0: Baja de 6–9 calls a una, pero sigue siendo una tool call exploratoria en cada pregunta y mete los 140 schemas enteros siempre. Es parchear con otra tool algo que es contenido.
why_wrong.2: Mezcla datos con la descripción de una acción: infla cada request y, en clientes como Claude Code, las descripciones largas se cortan. La descripción es para explicar la tool, no para cargar un catálogo.
why_wrong.3: Trata el síntoma (latencia) y deja las mismas llamadas exploratorias.

questions.rule: Catálogos, schemas y documentación = resources (los controla la app). Acciones = tools (las controla el modelo).
questions.source_quote: Passive data sources that provide read-only access to information for context, such as file contents, database schemas, or API documentation.

verification.notes: Doc MCP server-concepts: resources pasivos de solo lectura (schemas). Cita textual. Se acortó la correcta B (era la más larga: 170 vs 149–153).

questions.scenario: A SaaS company runs a nightly incident-summary job on a Linux CI runner: `claude -p "Using @runbooks:file://oncall/escalation, summarize last night's alerts"`. The `runbooks` MCP server, owned by the SRE team, exposes the runbooks only as resources, and `claude mcp list` on the runner shows it as `✔ Connected`. The summaries never follow the escalation runbook, and when asked, Claude says it was given no runbook content. The same prompt works perfectly in interactive sessions on developers' laptops. The SRE team will not add tools to their server. What should the job change?
options: Increase `MCP_TIMEOUT` on the runner, because in headless runs the resource is fetched before the server finishes connecting and the attachment comes back empty.
Ask the SRE team to declare the `subscribe` capability on the server so headless clients receive the runbook content through change notifications.
Replace the `@` mention with an instruction to read the `file://oncall/escalation` resource from `runbooks` with Claude Code's resource-reading tool.
Quote the mention as `@"runbooks:file://oncall/escalation"` so the headless prompt parser treats the whole URI as one resource reference.
questions.why_correct: En modo interactivo, un `@server:protocol://path` se busca y se adjunta solo. Pero con `claude -p`, la mención de un resource queda como texto plano. Claude Code igual le da a Claude tools para listar y leer resources MCP (`ListMcpResourcesTool`, `ReadMcpResourceTool`), así que pedirle que lea el resource por URI funciona sin tocar el server.

why_wrong.0: El server figura conectado; no es un problema de tiempo. En `-p` la mención directamente no se resuelve.
why_wrong.1: Las suscripciones avisan cuando un resource cambia; no hacen que una mención en texto plano se convierta en adjunto.
why_wrong.3: No hay una sintaxis de comillas documentada que cambie esto: en `-p` la mención queda como texto.

questions.rule: En `claude -p`, `@server:uri` es texto plano: pedí leer el resource con la tool de lectura de resources.
questions.source_quote: With `claude -p`, a resource mention stays plain text.

verification.notes: Doc mcp: con `claude -p` la mención de resource queda texto plano; Claude Code da tools para listar/leer resources. Cita textual. Se acortó la correcta C (173 vs 137–161).

questions.scenario: An airline built its own customer support host application with an MCP client. A `policies` MCP server exposes each fare-rule document as a resource (for example, `policy://fares/basic-economy`). Agents keep sessions open for a full shift, and the host reads the relevant policy resources at the start of each session. When the legal team updated the change-fee rules at 11:00, sessions opened earlier kept quoting the old fee until 18:00, generating 230 incorrect quotes. The server already declares `listChanged`. What is the most effective fix?
options: Have the host rely on the existing `listChanged` capability and re-read every policy resource whenever a list-changed notification arrives from the server.
Have the server declare `subscribe`, have the host subscribe to the policy resources it loaded, and re-read a resource when its update notification arrives.
Convert the policies into a `get_policy` tool so the model fetches a fresh copy every time it needs one, instead of relying on context loaded at session start.
Force agents to restart their sessions every hour so the host reloads the policy resources and the quotes never lag more than an hour behind changes.
questions.why_correct: MCP tiene suscripciones opcionales: el cliente se suscribe a resources específicos con `resources/subscribe` y recibe `notifications/resources/updated` cuando cambian. Eso resuelve el caso exacto: el documento cambió, la lista no.

why_wrong.0: Casi: `listChanged` avisa cuando cambia la LISTA de resources disponibles (se agregan o quitan), no cuando cambia el contenido de uno existente. Acá la lista es la misma.
why_wrong.2: Funcionaría a medias: vuelve exploratorio algo que es contenido y depende de que el modelo se acuerde de llamarla cada vez. Es usar una tool para leer datos.
why_wrong.3: Achica la ventana de error pero no la elimina, y le corta el trabajo a los agentes. Trata el síntoma.

questions.rule: Cambió el contenido de un resource → `subscribe` + `notifications/resources/updated`. Cambió la lista → `listChanged`.
questions.source_quote: The protocol supports optional subscriptions to resource changes. Clients can subscribe to specific resources and receive notifications when they change

verification.notes: Spec resources 2025-11-25: subscribe + notifications/resources/updated vs listChanged (lista). Cita textual.

questions.scenario: An accounts-payable company extracts line items from 8,000 invoices a day with an agent built on the API and its own MCP client. To normalize vendor names, the model calls the `lookup_vendor(name)` tool on the master-data server for each line, averaging 12 calls per invoice. The vendor master has 2,100 entries and changes weekly. The host application already embeds invoice text for routing. The team wants fewer exploratory calls and wants the application, not the model, to decide which vendors are relevant for each invoice. Which design should they adopt?
options: Expose a resource template `vendor://{name}` so the model reads one vendor per line through the resource interface instead of through a tool call.
Keep `lookup_vendor` but allow parallel tool calls, so the 12 lookups for each invoice run together in one turn instead of sequentially.
Cache each `lookup_vendor` result in the conversation history so repeated vendors on later invoices of the same batch don't need a new call.
Expose the vendor master as a resource; the host reads it, selects the entries relevant to each invoice with its embeddings, and passes them as context.
questions.why_correct: Los resources son application-driven: la aplicación puede acceder a la información y decidir cómo usarla, ya sea seleccionando porciones relevantes, buscando con embeddings o pasándola entera al modelo. Eso es justo lo que pide el equipo: el host elige los proveedores relevantes y el modelo ya los tiene en contexto, sin 12 lookups.

why_wrong.0: Un template parametrizado sigue siendo una lectura por proveedor y supone que alguien ya sabe el nombre exacto: no gana visibilidad, solo cambia la interfaz.
why_wrong.1: Baja la latencia, no la cantidad de llamadas exploratorias. Trata el síntoma.
why_wrong.2: Ayuda con repetidos dentro de un batch, pero sigue siendo el modelo descubriendo datos por tool calls e infla el historial.

questions.rule: Si la app debe decidir qué contexto entra (embeddings, filtros), exponé los datos como resource directo.
questions.source_quote: Applications can access this information directly and decide how to use it - whether that's selecting relevant portions, searching with embeddings, or passing it all to the model.

verification.notes: Doc server-concepts: la app decide cómo usar los resources (porciones, embeddings). Cita textual.

questions.scenario: A product analytics team built an MCP server for Claude Code so developers can ask about feature usage. Each dashboard is exposed as a resource with URI `ui://dashboards/<name>` and media type `text/html;profile=mcp-app`. The server declares the `resources` capability and implements `resources/list` and `resources/read`. Developers report that typing `@` shows none of the dashboards, and when they ask Claude to list the server's resources, it says the list is empty. The team's goal is for Claude to read the usage numbers, not to render the dashboards. What should they change?
options: Also expose the usage data as regular resources, such as `analytics://usage/<feature>` with `application/json`, next to the UI pages for the host.
Declare the `listChanged` capability so Claude Code refreshes the resource list after startup and the dashboards appear in the `@` autocomplete menu.
Convert each dashboard into a resource template, `ui://dashboards/{name}`, so Claude Code discovers them through the templates list instead of the plain list.
Add the `audience: ["assistant"]` annotation to each dashboard resource so Claude Code treats them as content for the model rather than for the user.
questions.why_correct: Los resources de MCP Apps (URI `ui://` o `text/html;profile=mcp-app`) son páginas para que la aplicación host las renderice, no contenido para que Claude lea. Claude Code los saca de las sugerencias de `@` y de la tool que lista resources; un server con solo UI resources muestra la lista vacía. Si querés que Claude lea los números, exponelos como resources de datos comunes.

why_wrong.1: `listChanged` sirve para avisar que la lista cambió; no hace que los UI resources pasen a aparecer.
why_wrong.2: Siguen siendo `ui://`: el problema es qué tipo de resource son, no si son directos o templates.
why_wrong.3: Las annotations son pistas para el cliente, pero no convierten una página para renderizar en contenido de datos ni cambian el filtro de Claude Code.

questions.rule: `ui://` / `text/html;profile=mcp-app` = página para el host. Datos para Claude = resource común.
questions.source_quote: MCP Apps UI resources are entries with a `ui://` URI or the `text/html;profile=mcp-app` media type: pages for a host application to render rather than content for Claude to read.

verification.notes: Doc mcp: UI resources ui:// o text/html;profile=mcp-app no aparecen en @ ni en la lista. Cita textual. Se acortó la correcta A (168 vs 149–158).

questions.scenario: A consulting firm runs a multi-agent research system. A coordinator spawns four search subagents per engagement against an internal `knowledge` MCP server that holds 3,500 prior reports. The server exposes `list_reports(filter)` and `get_report_metadata(id)` as tools. Token accounting shows 40% of each subagent's tokens go to calling these two tools just to learn which reports exist and what they cover, often for the same reports in parallel subagents. Final syntheses are good, but cost per engagement is 2.3 times the budget. What change most directly cuts this exploratory cost?
options: Give each subagent a larger context window and a higher turn limit, so it can finish exploring the catalog in fewer, longer turns before it starts the actual search.
Merge `list_reports` and `get_report_metadata` into a single `browse_reports` tool that returns the filtered list together with each report's metadata in one call.
Expose the report catalog and summaries as MCP resources; the coordinator reads them once and passes each subagent the entries relevant to its question.
Run the four subagents sequentially instead of in parallel, so later subagents can reuse the catalog exploration that earlier subagents already performed.
questions.why_correct: La guía del examen lo dice textual: exponer catálogos de contenido como resources MCP da a los agentes visibilidad de los datos disponibles sin tool calls exploratorias. El coordinador (la aplicación) lee el catálogo una vez y reparte lo relevante en el prompt de cada subagente.

why_wrong.0: Más contexto y turnos solo permiten explorar más, no menos: el costo sube.
why_wrong.1: Casi: baja de N llamadas a una por subagente, pero cada uno sigue explorando el catálogo por su cuenta. La guía apunta a resources para catálogos.
why_wrong.3: Sacrifica el paralelismo y el reuso depende de pasar contexto a mano; el catálogo sigue descubriéndose con tools.

questions.rule: ¿Los agentes gastan llamadas en averiguar qué hay? Ese catálogo va como resource.
questions.source_quote: Exposing content catalogs as MCP resources to give agents visibility into available data without requiring exploratory tool calls

verification.notes: Guía del examen: catálogos como resources para evitar tool calls exploratorias. Cita textual.

questions.scenario: A software company's internal developer portal connects a ticketing MCP server to its assistant. To "keep things simple", the server team modeled ticket creation as a resource template: reading `tickets://create?title={title}&team={team}` creates a ticket and returns its id. The portal's resource picker shows previews and performs automatic context inclusion based on heuristics. Since launch, the ticketing system has received 1,900 tickets in two weeks, about 60% of them duplicates or titled with fragments of what developers were typing. The server team wants ticket creation to happen only when the model decides to create one, with the option to require user approval. What should they do?
options: Keep the template but add the `priority: 0.0` annotation, so the portal treats the create resource as optional and stops including it automatically in context.
Keep the template and declare `subscribe`, so the portal reads the create resource only after it receives an update notification from the server.
Keep the template but require an extra `confirm=true` parameter in the URI, so heuristic reads without that parameter return a preview instead of a ticket.
Replace the template with a `create_ticket` tool, since tools are model-controlled actions that can change state and clients can put a human in the loop.
questions.why_correct: Los resources son datos pasivos de solo lectura y los maneja la aplicación (pickers, inclusión automática): cualquier lectura puede pasar sin que el modelo lo decida. Las acciones con efecto (crear, escribir, llamar APIs) son tools, que controla el modelo y que el cliente puede someter a aprobación humana.

why_wrong.0: Las annotations son pistas; la app puede leer el resource igual. Una lectura con efectos sigue siendo un diseño roto.
why_wrong.1: Las suscripciones son para cambios de contenido; no convierten una lectura en una acción controlada por el modelo.
why_wrong.2: Parchea el síntoma dentro de un diseño equivocado: un resource no debería tener efectos y sigue sin haber control del modelo ni aprobación.

questions.rule: Si leerlo cambia algo, no es un resource: es una tool.
questions.source_quote: Functions that your LLM can actively call, and decides when to use them based on user requests. Tools can write to databases, call external APIs, modify files, or trigger other logic.

verification.notes: Doc server-concepts: tools model-controlled, pueden escribir/llamar APIs; priority es annotation de la spec. Cita textual.

questions.scenario: A hardware vendor built a support agent with its own MCP client. Its `kb` server exposes 4,000 troubleshooting articles through three resource templates (`kb://articles/{id}`, `kb://products/{sku}/faq`, `kb://errors/{code}`) and declares the `resources` capability. On startup, the host calls `resources/list`, receives an empty array, and concludes the knowledge base is unavailable, so the agent answers from general knowledge. The server team says the templates are working when they test with the MCP Inspector. Listing every article as a direct resource would make the list enormous. What should the host change?
options: Call `resources/templates/list` to discover the parameterized templates, then read concrete URIs built from them with `resources/read`.
Ask the server team to expose all 4,000 articles as direct resources, so `resources/list` returns them and the host can show them in its picker.
Ask the server team to declare `listChanged`, so the host receives a notification with the templates once the server finishes indexing articles.
Wrap the knowledge base in a `search_kb` tool on the host side, so the model searches articles itself whenever the resource list comes back empty.
questions.why_correct: `resources/list` devuelve los resources directos. Los resource templates (URIs parametrizadas) se descubren aparte con `resources/templates/list`, y después leés una URI concreta con `resources/read`. El host simplemente no estaba preguntando por los templates.

why_wrong.1: Funcionaría, pero es justo lo que la restricción quiere evitar: una lista gigante. Para datos parametrizados existen los templates.
why_wrong.2: `listChanged` avisa cambios en la lista de resources; no reemplaza la llamada que descubre templates.
why_wrong.3: Esquiva el problema convirtiendo contenido en exploración por tools, y el host sigue sin descubrir los templates.

questions.source_quote: Resource templates allow servers to expose parameterized resources using URI templates.

verification.notes: Spec resources: templates parametrizados vía resources/templates/list. Cita textual.

questions.scenario: A bank's architecture team uses Claude Code for developer productivity. The `adr` MCP server exposes 600 architecture decision records only as resources. A `design-reviewer` subagent is defined with `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, mcp__adr__*` so it can consult past decisions. In the main conversation, Claude lists and reads ADR resources without problems. Inside `design-reviewer`, Claude says it cannot access any ADRs and reviews designs without precedent. The `/mcp` panel shows `adr` connected. What change lets the subagent read the ADRs while keeping its tool list minimal?
options: Replace `mcp__adr__*` with `mcp__adr` in the `tools` field, because a server-level entry is needed to grant access to everything the server exposes, including resources.
Add `ListMcpResourcesTool` and `ReadMcpResourceTool` to the subagent's `tools`, since resources are read through those built-in tools, not through `mcp__adr__` tools.
Add the `adr` server to the subagent's `mcpServers` field by name, so the subagent opens its own connection and receives the server's resources at startup.
Remove the `tools` field from the subagent so it inherits all tools, because resource access is only granted to subagents that inherit the full parent pool.
questions.why_correct: En Claude Code los resources se listan y leen con tools built-in: `ListMcpResourcesTool` y `ReadMcpResourceTool`. Un server que solo expone resources no tiene tools `mcp__adr__*`, así que ese wildcard no le da nada. Con un allowlist, tenés que nombrar esas dos tools; los nombres de tools son los mismos strings que usás en las listas de los subagentes.

why_wrong.0: `mcp__adr` vs. `mcp__adr__*` es la forma de referirse a las TOOLS del server; ninguna de las dos cubre resources si el server no tiene tools.
why_wrong.2: Una referencia por nombre en `mcpServers` comparte la conexión del padre, pero no agrega al allowlist las tools que leen resources.
why_wrong.3: Heredar todo lo arreglaría, pero rompe la restricción de lista mínima: le da `Edit`, `Bash`, etc.

questions.rule: Resources en Claude Code = `ListMcpResourcesTool` + `ReadMcpResourceTool`. Si el subagente tiene allowlist, nombralas.
questions.source_quote: | `ReadMcpResourceTool` | Reads a specific MCP resource by URI | No |

verification.notes: Doc tools-reference: ListMcpResourcesTool/ReadMcpResourceTool built-in; mcp: referencia por nombre en mcpServers comparte conexión. Cita textual.

questions.scenario: A logistics company's developers use Claude Code with an internal `warehouse` MCP server. Its `dump_schema` tool returns the DDL of all 300 tables, about 180,000 characters, every time a developer asks about one or two tables. Each result is saved to a file and replaced in the conversation by a path, and Claude then reads chunks of the file, which takes several extra steps. A developer already raised `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` to 100,000 and nothing changed. The team wants developers to bring exactly the tables they care about into the prompt. What is the best change to the server?
options: Set `_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]` to 200,000 on `dump_schema`, so its full result stays inline in the conversation instead of being saved to a file.
Ask developers to raise `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` further, to 200,000, because the current value is still below the size of the full schema output.
Expose each table's schema as a resource, such as `schema://orders`, so developers reference `@warehouse:schema://orders` and only that table is attached.
Paginate `dump_schema` with a `page` parameter that returns 20 tables at a time, so each result stays under the size at which results are saved to a file.
questions.why_correct: Un schema es contenido de solo lectura: como resource por tabla, el developer lo referencia con `@warehouse:schema://orders` y Claude Code lo busca y lo adjunta automáticamente. Entra solo lo que importa, sin tool calls ni archivos intermedios.

why_wrong.0: Esa annotation existe y dejaría el resultado inline, pero mete 180.000 caracteres en cada pregunta sobre una tabla. Resuelve el archivo, no el desperdicio.
why_wrong.1: Más allá del tamaño, la doc aclara que un resultado de texto de más de 50.000 caracteres se guarda a archivo igual y que `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` no cambia ese umbral. Por eso no pasó nada.
why_wrong.3: Evita el archivo, pero el modelo tiene que paginar explorando hasta dar con sus tablas: más tool calls exploratorias.

questions.rule: Contenido que el usuario elige (schemas, docs) → resource referenciable con `@server:uri`.
questions.source_quote: Resources are automatically fetched and included as attachments when referenced

verification.notes: Doc mcp: resources referenciados se adjuntan solos; resultado >50.000 caracteres a archivo y MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS no cambia el umbral; maxResultSizeChars existe. Cita textual.

questions.scenario: A legal-tech startup runs a multi-agent research system with its own MCP host. The `contracts` server's `search_contracts(query)` tool now returns `resource_link` items (URI, name, description) instead of full contract text, which cut context usage by 70%. However, a safety layer in the host validates every link by checking that its URI appears in the server's `resources/list` before reading it. Since the change, 85% of search results are discarded as "unknown resource", and the synthesis agent reports that no relevant contracts were found. What should the team change?
options: Have the server also return the full contract text alongside each link, so the host can fall back to the embedded text whenever validation discards a link.
Have the server register every contract it might return as a direct resource, so `resources/list` always contains every URI that a search could produce.
Switch the host validation to compare against `resources/templates/list` instead, since links returned by tools are always instances of a declared template.
Drop the host check against `resources/list` and fetch each returned link by its URI, since links returned by tools aren't guaranteed to be listed.
questions.why_correct: La spec de MCP lo aclara: una tool PUEDE devolver links a resources, y los resource links que devuelven las tools no tienen garantía de aparecer en `resources/list`. La validación del host asume algo que el protocolo no promete; el cliente lee el link directamente por su URI.

why_wrong.0: Vuelve a meter el texto completo y pierde el 70% de ahorro que motivó el cambio.
why_wrong.1: Obliga al server a listar miles de contratos para satisfacer una validación incorrecta del host.
why_wrong.2: La spec no dice que los links devueltos por tools sean siempre instancias de un template declarado.

questions.rule: Un `resource_link` devuelto por una tool se lee por su URI; no tiene por qué estar en `resources/list`.
questions.source_quote: Resource links returned by tools are not guaranteed to appear in the results of a `resources/list` request.

verification.notes: Spec tools 2025-11-25: resource links de tools no garantizados en resources/list. Cita casi textual (en la página está partida por el `>` de la nota markdown). Se acortó la correcta D (166 vs 152–156).
